subject: Runtime dependency keystore residency & subprocessor ownership — evidence request
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@medsecure.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@medsecure.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: runtime keystore residency + subprocessor ownership details (SOC2 / SIG follow-up)

Hi Kimberly,

Following up on our SOC 2 intake and SIG review. We need a concise package that answers the following scoped to runtime dependencies (not the full stack):

1) Canonical list of subprocessor services involved in runtime tokenization/kv cache/ephemeral key management/metrics that may handle customer-derived secrets or crypto material. For each processor, indicate: name, function (e.g., KV cache, metrics ingestion), data types processed, and country of processing/residency.

2) Proof of KMS residency and control path for keys used in Hosted vs Dedicated deployments (who holds key material, any split-keystore patterns, and whether keys ever persist outside customer-owned KMS).

3) Rotation/TTL policy for ephemeral keys used in model inference and an example rotation log for one recent rotation event.

Target: we need evidence we can include in our SIG intake and provide to our internal audit team next week. If you can provide a single bundle (CSV roster + short PDF callout + rotation matrix), that would be ideal.

Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? If helpful, we can take a short 30-minute call to walk through.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Security Engineering Manager
MedSecure Health

--
MedSecure Security Intake Portal: security@medsecure.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@medsecure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: runtime keystore residency + subprocessor ownership details (SOC2 / SIG follow-up)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the clear scope — we can assemble that. High level answers up front:

- We will provide a subprocessor roster scoped to runtime components (KV caches, feature stores used for batching, metrics pipeline, ephemeral key orchestration, and any third-party telemetry that touches request identifiers).
- KMS residency: for Hosted API, Redwood-managed KMS keys are used for platform operational secrets; customer data keys are envelope-encrypted and can be stored in customer KMS for Dedicated/Private. We will include a short provenance PDF that documents key custody and the control path for both deployment modes.
- Ephemeral key rotation: default TTL is 1 hour for inference session keys; rotation events are audited and we will include a sanitized rotation log sample.

Attachments I will send in this thread: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260818.csv, kms_provenance_summary_20260818.pdf, ephemeral_key_rotation_matrix.xlsx.

Action items for us: Ben will validate the residency column for each subprocessor and Marissa will sanitize the rotation log for sharing. We expect to deliver the bundle by EOD Wednesday (2026-08-19). If that doesn't work for your audit timeline, please let us know and we can prioritize.

If you'd like a call, a 30-minute window tomorrow 10:00–10:30am PT works for us.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20260818.csv (CSV listing of runtime subprocessors), kms_provenance_summary_20260818.pdf (2-page provenance + diagram), ephemeral_key_rotation_matrix.xlsx (rotation policy + sample rows)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@medsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: runtime keystore residency + subprocessor ownership details (SOC2 / SIG follow-up)

Kimberly / Aisha — quick clarifications from the runtime side:

- "KV cache" items in the roster include both in-memory, ephemeral caches we run on-host and an optional managed Redis instance we offer for large customers. For managed Redis the data-in-flight is TLS; persisted data is encrypted-at-rest with platform keys unless the customer uses Dedicated and brings their own KMS. I'll mark the residency column accordingly.

- Metrics pipeline: we separate traces/metrics from request payloads; the metrics collector only receives anonymized identifiers (no PII or customer plain-text prompt content). We'll call that out in the CSV details.

- Ephemeral key example: I'll replace real IDs with hashed placeholders in the rotation sample so it remains useful for audit without exposing secrets.

I'll drop a final validated CSV and the sanitized rotation matrix by 17:00 PT.

Ben
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
